lesson.text: Quick memory: in grade 3, what is the imaginary line around the middle of the Earth called? (The Equator.) Today: an invisible grid of lines that gives every place on Earth its own address.
Lines of latitude run across the globe, east to west, like the rungs of a ladder. They measure how far north or south of the Equator a place is: from 0° at the Equator to 90°N and 90°S at the Poles.
Lines of longitude run from pole to pole. They measure how far east or west a place is from the Prime Meridian, 0°, which runs through Greenwich in London. They go up to 180°, east and west.
A place's address is its latitude, then its longitude. Quito in Ecuador is at about 0°, 78°W: on the Equator, west of Greenwich. Singapore is at about 1°N, 104°E, and London at about 51.5°N, 0°.

The Equator splits Earth into the northern and southern hemispheres; the Prime Meridian and the 180° line split it into the western and eastern. Sydney, at about 34°S, 151°E, is in the southern and eastern hemispheres.

Two special lines of latitude are the Tropic of Cancer, about 23.5°N, and the Tropic of Capricorn, about 23.5°S. Between them, the Sun is right overhead at noon on at least one day a year. This hot band is the tropics.
The Arctic Circle, about 66.5°N, and the Antarctic Circle, about 66.5°S, mark the polar regions. Inside them, there is at least one day each year when the Sun never sets, and one when it never rises.
Try it in the world: mark a grid in your world with fence lines every 10 blocks, and number them from a centre line. Give each of your builds its grid address. Next: time zones.

exercises.hint: Latitude is measured north and south from it.

exercises.prompt: Through which city does the Prime Meridian run?
exercises.explain: Greenwich is in London, so the Prime Meridian runs through London.

exercises.prompt: Lines of latitude run from the North Pole to the South Pole.
exercises.hint: Which lines are like the rungs of a ladder?
exercises.explain: False: lines of latitude run across, east to west. Lines of longitude run from pole to pole.

exercises.prompt: What is the latitude of the North Pole?
exercises.hint: Latitude goes from 0° at the Equator up to the poles.
exercises.explain: The North Pole is at 90°N, as far north as you can go.

exercises.prompt: A place at 30°S is south of the Equator.
exercises.hint: What does the S stand for?
exercises.explain: True: S means south of the Equator.

exercises.prompt: Sort these cities: north or south of the Equator?
exercises.hint: Look at the letter after each latitude: N or S.
exercises.explain: N: Cairo, Tokyo, Oslo. S: Sydney, Lima, Cape Town.

exercises.hint: The two tropics are at 23.5°, one north and one south.
exercises.explain: The Tropic of Cancer is at about 23.5°N; Capricorn is at about 23.5°S.

exercises.prompt: Match each line to its latitude.
exercises.hint: Start at 0° and move out towards the poles.
exercises.explain: Equator 0°, Tropic of Capricorn about 23.5°S, Arctic Circle about 66.5°N, North Pole 90°N.

exercises.prompt: Place B on the map is in the eastern hemisphere.
exercises.hint: Read B's longitude: E or W of the Prime Meridian?
exercises.explain: True: B is at 120°E, east of the Prime Meridian.

exercises.prompt: What does longitude tell you about a place?
exercises.hint: Longitude lines run from pole to pole.
choices: how far east or west of Greenwich it is
how far north or south it is
how high above the sea it is
how far it is from a city
exercises.explain: Longitude measures how far east or west of the Prime Meridian, at Greenwich, a place is.

exercises.prompt: Which city is in both the southern and the western hemispheres?
exercises.hint: You need S for the latitude and W for the longitude.
exercises.explain: Buenos Aires: 35°S is south of the Equator and 58°W is west of Greenwich.

exercises.prompt: Where is the Sun right overhead at noon on at least one day a year?
exercises.hint: Think of the band between 23.5°N and 23.5°S.
exercises.explain: Between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn: the tropics.

exercises.prompt: Place A is at 40°N and place B is at 20°S. How many degrees of latitude apart are they?
exercises.hint: Count from A down to the Equator, then on to B.
exercises.explain: From 40°N to the Equator is 40°; from the Equator to 20°S is 20° more. 40 + 20 = 60°.

exercises.prompt: Inside the Arctic Circle, there is at least one day a year when the Sun does not set.
exercises.hint: What makes the polar circles special?
exercises.explain: True: inside the polar circles there is at least one day without a sunset and one without a sunrise.

exercises.prompt: A ship sails from 10°N to 30°N. Which line does it cross?
exercises.hint: Which special line lies between 10°N and 30°N?
exercises.explain: The Tropic of Cancer, at about 23.5°N.

exercises.prompt: Sort the cities: eastern or western hemisphere?
exercises.hint: E means east of the Prime Meridian; W means west of it.
exercises.explain: East: Singapore, Sydney and Cairo. West: Quito, Buenos Aires and Lima, all in South America.

exercises.prompt: Order the lines of latitude from north to south.
exercises.hint: Start at about 66.5°N and work down through 0° to about 66.5°S.
exercises.explain: The Arctic Circle (about 66.5°N), the Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N), the Equator (0°), the Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S), then the Antarctic Circle (66.5°S).

exercises.prompt: Place A is at 30°E and place B is at 45°W. How many degrees of longitude apart are they?
exercises.hint: Count from 30°E to the Prime Meridian, then on to 45°W.
exercises.explain: From 30°E to 0° is 30°, and from 0° to 45°W is 45° more: 30 + 45 = 75°.
